summary: Monika Zin is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. She studied at Jagiellonian University, the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, and the University of Munich. She held professorships at Munich (~1994–2016) and Free University of Berlin (~2014–2015).

Montgomery Schuyler specialized in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Columbia University under A. V. Williams Jackson from roughly 1895 to 1902 and subsequently served as a fellow at Columbia University from 1900 to 1902.
Moodeen Sheriff worked in Indology and other fields. He was educated at Madras Medical College and later served as Native Surgeon at the Triplicane Dispensary from 1858 to 1889.

Moreton John Walhouse worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the East India Company College (1841–1842) and served in the Indian Civil Service (~1840–1873), including as Judge of Mangalore in the Madras Presidency (~1870–1873).

Moriichi Yamazaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University and the University of Cambridge under K. R. Norman. He served as a professor at Sendai National College of Technology (~1985–2004) and president at Hosen Gakuen College (~2004).

Moritz Abraham Stern was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Göttingen under Carl Friedrich Gauss and Karl Otfried Müller, later serving as an extraordinarius professor at Göttingen from 1829 to 1884.

Moritz Spitzer was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Vienna and Kiel University under Friedrich Otto Schrader, completing his Ph.D. between 1923 and 1926. He subsequently served as an assistant at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1927 to 1928.

Moritz Steinschneider worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied under Franz Bopp and Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer, earning his PhD at the University of Leipzig (~1850). His career included serving as director of the Jüdische Mädchenschule Berlin (1869–1890).

Moriz Haupt was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at the University of Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann, later serving there as privatdozent and professor (1837–1851), followed by an appointment as professor of Roman literature at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1853.

Moriz Winternitz was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna under Georg Bühler and under Friedrich Max Müller. He taught at Oxford and later served as professor at the German University in Prague (1902–1934).

Morris Swadesh was a linguist who studied at the University of Chicago and Yale University under Leonard Bloomfield and Edward Sapir. He held academic posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1937–1939) and the National Autonomous University of Mexico (1956–1967).

Morten Schlütter works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Copenhagen, Komazawa University, and Yale University under Stanley Weinstein, Birthe Arendrup, and Shudo Ishii. He has served as an associate professor at the University of Iowa.

Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at University College London and the University of London under Alfred Edward Housman. He directed the National Museum Cardiff and the London Museum, and was Director-General of Archæology in India (1944–1948).

Morton Klass worked in religious studies, Indology, and other fields. He studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University, and under Conrad M. Arensberg. He served as a professor at Barnard College and Columbia University from approximately 1965 to 1997.

Morton W. Easton worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Columbia University and Yale University, where his doctoral supervisor was William Dwight Whitney. He was a professor at the University of Tennessee (1871–1881) and the University of Pennsylvania (1882–1912).
Mother Sayamagyi was active in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She was a disciple of and succeeded Sayagyi U Ba Khin, and later taught Roger Bischoff.

Motohiro Yoritomi was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama, and under Motoshin Yoritomi. He was a professor at Shuchiin University (1976; emeritus 2002–2011) and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (1998).

Motoi Ono is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher. He studied under Yasunori Ejima at the University of Tsukuba and earned his Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna. He became an associate professor at the University of Tsukuba around 1996.
Moumita Hossain works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Ranjit Sen and is attested in 2026 as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society.

Mountstuart Elphinstone worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After attending the Royal High School (~1791–1794), he served the East India Company (~1795–1799), became an envoy at Kabul University (~1808–1809), and was Governor at the University of Mumbai (1819–1827).
